Keep track of what matters to you with tools you put together yourself, and an AI that can read them, fill them in and set them up with you.
A demo is waiting: twelve weeks in the life of Camille, to see what the app looks like once built.
The Guide is the book at the top of the home screen.
The journey is over: the rest is yours to do in the order you like.
What comes next waits in the Guide, the book at the top of the home screen.
This tutorial begins in the demo. Reinstall it, or skip its steps there.
These tutorials use the demo: %1$s. Without it, their steps in the demo are skipped. You can reinstall it at any time from Settings › Demo.
A look at the demo, then your own zone and your first tool. No AI needed.
You have a zone of your own and a tool that keeps your entries. Next: an AI to work with you.
The demo follows Camille, who trains for a half marathon. A zone is one area of a life: here, running. Its tools are sorted in groups: Training, Body, Analysis.
Runs is a Tracking tool: each entry is a figure, here kilometres, with its date. The + adds one; the buttons under the title are ready-made entries.
Your run is already in the chart, and the goal « Training week » counted it. Tools feed each other: a chart, a goal, a variable read the entries of other tools.
On the home screen, the + of a group creates a zone: give it a name, an icon, a short description. Outside the demo: what you add to the demo goes at the next update.
In your zone, the + of a section lists the tool types. Any will do; Tracking is the simplest: a figure, a rating, a choice, a timer.
Note a first entry in it
Open your tool and add an entry. A touch and hold on a tool\'s title opens its configuration, to change it at any time.
The AI has the same moves as you: it reads your tools, fills them in, sets them up. It needs a key from a provider, which you bring.
The AI is connected. Next: have it build with you.
The settings hold the providers: Claude, OpenAI, DeepSeek, or any service that speaks like OpenAI\'s API (Ollama, LM Studio…).
Set up a provider with your key
Touch a provider, paste the API key you created on its site, choose a model, save. The key stays on your phone and goes only to that provider.
Each exchange with the AI is paid to the provider, by your key. The conversation shows what each one cost. Settings › AI limits caps how far the AI goes alone.
Open the conversation (the speech bubble). In your message, add a pointer to your tool: it attaches its entries over a period. Ask « what do you make of my entries? ». Then Next.
Describe what you want to follow: the AI creates the tools and links them. You stay in charge: it shows what it does.
The AI built a tool and a variable with you. Next: have it work on its own, on a schedule.
The AI creates and sets up tools, adds entries, writes variables, as you would. When it lacks something, it asks you as a field to fill in.
Ask the AI to create a tool
In the conversation, point to your zone and describe what you want to follow: « a tracking of my water, in glasses ». The step is done when the AI has created it, not you.
Look at the tool it made
Close the conversation and open the new tool: it is a tool like any other, which you can change by its configuration.
Have it link two tools by a variable
Ask for a figure drawn from your entries: « a variable with the glasses of the day ». A goal or a chart can then read it.
Choose what it must ask before doing
Settings › AI validation: the AI can be made to show each change and wait for your approval, for the app, a zone, a tool or a conversation. Then Next.
An automation has the AI work on its own, on a schedule: a weekly summary, a reminder that reads your entries.
Your automation runs on its schedule; its history keeps every run. The Guide\'s reference holds the rest, in the order you like.
An automation is a starting message to the AI, with its attachments, sent on a schedule. The AI then acts as in a conversation, alone, within the limits you set.
Create an automation in a zone
In a zone, the + of a section offers « Automation »: name it, give it a schedule (every Sunday at 6 pm), then write its starting message: « sum up my week ».
On the automation\'s card in its zone, the test button runs it now, without waiting for its schedule.
The automation\'s history keeps each run: what the AI read, did and answered, and what it cost. Then Next.
